question.text: Which of the following is NOT a condition for a derivative contract to receive legal validity under SCRA?

answer.text: The derivative must be traded on both domestic and international exchanges simultaneously
The derivative must be traded on a recognized stock exchange
The derivative must be settled on the clearing house of the recognized stock exchange
The contract must comply with the rules and bye-laws of the exchange

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 18A, the source-stated conditions for legal validity are that the contract is traded on a recognized stock exchange, that it is settled through the clearing house of that exchange in accordance with its rules and bye-laws, and that the contract relates to parties and terms covered by the Central Government notification. Simultaneous trading on domestic and international exchanges is not one of those conditions. The Trap: Recognised-exchange trading, clearing-house settlement under exchange rules and bye-laws, and the Central Government notification condition are all positive requirements; only the simultaneous domestic-and-international trading option lies outside Section 18A. Note: Section 18A should be read as a multi-condition test rather than as a simple two-part requirement, so all source-stated conditions need to be present for legal validity.
